statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit across five representative archetypes/journeys.

page.framework: Server-rendered legacy Django-style MPA with custom JavaScript/JW Player
page.notes: Persian RTL public video-sharing site. Homepage, video, playlist, search, and login were sampled.

paths.description: Homepage and long discovery feed: core browse journey, preferences, performance, security, sustainability, mobile layout, and crawler rendering.
Representative video detail/player: core watch journey, metadata, media accessibility, delayed startup, mobile reflow, and crawler rendering.
News playlist: category/listing template and visual hierarchy.
Search results for آموزش: primary discovery flow, listing template, mobile reflow, and non-JS content.
Account login and blank-submit recovery: labels, autofill, validation, privacy and recovery affordances.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in theme to the normal capture, and the CSS probe found zero color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface, text, control, and media colors using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Navigation changes have no View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The live CSS probe found zero view-transition rules despite the browser exposing document.startViewTransition.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for route/template changes, with a non-animated fallback.

findings.summary: The long discovery feed provides no scroll-linked progress or entry feedback.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 23,704px tall at mobile size, while the CSS probe found no animation-timeline or scroll-timeline rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use restrained scroll-driven progress or entry feedback where it helps orientation, and disable non-essential motion under reduced motion.

findings.summary: The very long homepage lacks scroll-state-aware orientation.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout measured a 23,704px document; recon and CSS probes found no scroll progress or scroll-state treatment in the page chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a subtle progress/orientation affordance or a compact scroll-aware header while keeping content dominant.

findings.summary: Repeated action menus are custom div dialogs rather than semantic top-layer primitives.
findings.evidence: The platform probe enumerated many div.action-menu elements with role=dialog, no dialog element, and no popover attribute.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement these menus with popover or dialog, declarative invokers, focus handling, Escape, and light dismiss.

findings.summary: Slow visual completion delays the core browse/watch experience.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.5s, FCP 3.4s, Speed Index 16.6s, and TTI 10.3s (performance 0.68); the trace observed a late LCP at 32.8s under its network run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the true LCP asset, compress responsive previews, and keep non-critical player/identity work out of the initial critical path.

findings.summary: Preview images and scripts are delivered inefficiently.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 100/100 legacy-format images, 51 without srcset, 49 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and four oversized images. HAR transferred 1.99MB, including 1.13MB images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants with width/height and sizes/srcset, lazy-load below-fold previews, and reserve eager/fetchpriority=high for the actual LCP image.

findings.summary: ARIA and accessible-name failures affect repeated controls.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found aria-expanded on a roleless div and repeated “مشاهده همه” links whose aria-label excludes their visible text; accessibility score was 0.86.
findings.suggestedFix: Put state ARIA on the controlling button, use semantic controls, and ensure each accessible name contains the visible label plus useful context.

findings.summary: Repeated links and footer text miss WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured the blue “مشاهده همه” links at 2.92:1 on #f8f9fa (4.5:1 required), with additional footer text at 4.44:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use text colors that meet at least 4.5:1 for normal text in every supported theme and preference mode.

findings.summary: Many feed action targets are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse and the live target probe found repeated 20x20px more-menu buttons, below even Lighthouse’s 24px minimum and well below a comfortable 44px touch area.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the interactive hit area and spacing while preserving visible density; retain clear focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: Google Identity emits console errors on ordinary homepage load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a FedCM NetworkError and “Not signed in with the identity provider” on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Load identity code only where needed and treat expected signed-out/FedCM rejection as a handled state rather than a console error.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: Header evidence found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, or Permissions-Policy. All three observed cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None; response also discloses very old Django/Python server versions.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, CSP including frame-ancestors, nosniff, a restrictive Permissions-Policy and Referrer-Policy; mark HTTPS cookies Secure and select the least-permissive SameSite value. Remove version disclosure.

findings.summary: Analytics and identity integrations add a broad third-party footprint without visible contextual disclosure.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics; HAR attributed 33 of 35 requests and 1.95MB to origins outside www.namasha.com (mostly Namasha CDNs, plus Google), and analytics cookies persist for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Document and minimise tracking, gate non-essential analytics by valid consent where required, shorten retention, and load identity providers only in context.

findings.summary: The site advertises standalone installation but has no offline/runtime support.
findings.evidence: A valid standalone manifest is linked, but the runtime probe found zero service-worker registrations and no named caches.
findings.suggestedFix: Either add a service worker with a tested offline fallback and resilient navigation handling, or stop presenting the site as installable.

findings.summary: The Persian RTL direction is only applied through CSS, not document semantics.
findings.evidence: html has lang=fa-IR but an empty dir attribute; computed body direction is rtl.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir=rtl on the html element so direction is available before CSS and to assist user agents, translation tools, and embedded components.

findings.summary: Login validation errors are not announced as status messages.
findings.evidence: Blank submission produced clear Persian field messages, but none had role=alert or aria-live and fields did not expose aria-invalid.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate each message with its field, set aria-invalid after validation, move focus to the first error or summary, and announce the summary with a live region.

findings.summary: The media-heavy homepage sends avoidable bytes for previews below the fold.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 1.99MB on initial load, 1.13MB in images; 100 images use legacy formats, 49 below-fold images are eager, and 51 lack responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt responsive AVIF/WebP pipelines, lazy loading, CDN transforms, and a page-weight budget for feed templates.

findings.summary: The sampled video has no captions or subtitle track.
findings.evidence: The playable video reached readyState 4 and played, but both player and metadata probes found zero track elements for a 6:22 spoken/animated video.
findings.suggestedFix: Require timed captions for uploaded speech-bearing video and expose caption selection through an accessible player control.

findings.summary: The conventional sitemap URL returns an HTML 404 page.
findings.evidence: GET /sitemap.xml returned an HTML document and HEAD confirmed HTTP 404, while robots.txt declares no alternative Sitemap location.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a valid XML sitemap (or sitemap index), return 200 with an XML content type, and declare its absolute URL in robots.txt.

taskList.title: Fix security headers and cookie policy
Build a responsive modern image pipeline and loading policy
Add captions to video publishing and playback
Correct ARIA names, roles, menu semantics, and touch targets
Add semantic RTL direction and announced login errors
Minimise and contextualise analytics/identity third parties
Publish and declare a valid sitemap
Add restrained route and scroll orientation affordances
